body.statement: For the exact published one-proxy map \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}}\), the class of \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\) is nonzero in \(\mathbb F[\mathbf m]/\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}\), and the additional relation \(R_{\mathrm{el}}=\beta W_2^{\mathrm{el}}-W_3^{\mathrm{el}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal I_{\le3}\). In the stated localization, \(\beta-W_3^{\mathrm{el}}/W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\in\mathcal I_{\le3}^{(W)}\); after quotienting by the localized observable ideal and extending to the observable function field, \[\mathcal I_{\le3}K_{\mathrm{obs}}[\beta]=\left\langle\beta-\frac{W_3^{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}\right\rangle.\] Therefore the generic full covariance-and-cubic fiber of \(\beta\) has degree one on \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\ne0\). Once the pinned checkpoint is established, this is a strict generic tightening of the nonidentification conclusion in Tramontano et al. (2025), Theorem 3.6, on the same parameterized moment map.
body.justification: The theorem turns an independently derived cubic contraction into a precisely testable statement about the exact released full ideal and its observable localization.
body.gap: Tramontano et al. (2025), Theorem 3.6, reports generic nonidentification through order three; the unreported object tested here is the localized full-ideal relation \(\beta W_2^{\mathrm{el}}-W_3^{\mathrm{el}}=0\) under the exact published parameterization.
body.consumer: The result determines whether the one-proxy implementation may use a generic cubic effect chart on \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\ne0\), subject to the pinned replication gate.
body.proof_tex:
First we verify that the localization denominator is not zero in the observable coordinate ring.  Choose the rational parameter point
\[
\gamma _1=\gamma _2=\gamma _3=u=\beta=1,qquad
\omega_j^{(2)}=\omega_j^{(3)}=1\quad(0\leq j\leq3).
\]
No positivity or probabilistic realizability condition is needed here because the ideals in Definitions~\(\mathrm{def{:}full\text{-}published\text{-}moment\text{-}ideal}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}elimination\text{-}ideal}\) are algebraic graph ideals with unrestricted cumulant coordinates.  Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}mixing\text{-}map}\) gives
\[
\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}}
=\begin{pmatrix}
1&1&0&0\\
2&1&1&0\\
3&1&1&1
\end{pmatrix}
\]
and therefore
\[
\mathbf c=(2,3,4,5,7,10,10,14,20,30).
\]
Substitution in the displayed definition of \(N^{\mathrm{el}}\) yields
\[
N^{\mathrm{el}}
=\begin{pmatrix}
3\cdot7-4\cdot5\\
3\cdot4-2\cdot7\\
2\cdot5-3^2
\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}1\\-2\\1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus
\[
W_2^{\mathrm{el}}=5(1)+10(-2)+14(1)=-1,
\qquad
W_3^{\mathrm{el}}=7(1)+14(-2)+20(1)=-1.
\]
This point lies in the parameterized image by construction.  Every element of \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}\) vanishes on that image, whereas \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\) evaluates to \(-1\).  Therefore
\[
W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\notin\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}},
\]
so its class is nonzero in \(\mathbb F[\mathbf m]/\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}\).  This also proves that the principal chart \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\ne0\) is nonempty.

We next justify all domain and properness assertions needed for division.  Let
\[
T=\mathbb F[\beta,\gamma _1,\gamma _2,\gamma _3,u,
\omega_0^{(2)},\ldots,\omega_3^{(2)},
\omega_0^{(3)},\ldots,\omega_3^{(3)}].
\]
Define \(\rho:\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pub}}\to T\) to fix the parameter variables and to send each of the sixteen moment variables to its polynomial moment formula in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}mixing\text{-}map}\).  Each generator of \(\mathcal J_{\leq3}\) is a moment variable minus its image, so \(\mathcal J_{\leq3}\subseteq\ker\rho\).  Conversely, successive polynomial division by these sixteen monic, distinct-leading-variable equations writes every \(F\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pub}}\) uniquely as
\[
F=G+F_0,qquad G\in\mathcal J_{\leq3},\quad F_0\in T,
\]
and \(\rho(F)=F_0\).  Hence \(\ker\rho=\mathcal J_{\leq3}\), and the first isomorphism theorem gives
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pub}}/\mathcal J_{\leq3}\cong T.
\]
Because \(T\) is a polynomial ring over the field \(\mathbb F=\mathbb Q\), it is an integral domain.  Therefore \(\mathcal J_{\leq3}\) is prime.  The contractions
\[
\mathcal I_{\leq3}=\mathcal J_{\leq3}\cap\mathbb F[\beta,\mathbf m],
\qquad
\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}=\mathcal I_{\leq3}\cap\mathbb F[\mathbf m]
\]
are consequently prime as well.  In particular
\[
A:=\mathbb F[\mathbf m]/\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}
\]
is an integral domain and its fraction field is the defined field \(K_{\mathrm{obs}}\).

By Proposition~\(\mathrm{prop{:}pinned\text{-}full\text{-}basis\text{-}checkpoint}\), exact division by the Gröbner basis of \(\mathcal I_{\leq3}\) has zero remainder.  Hence
\[
R_{\mathrm{el}}=\beta W_2^{\mathrm{el}}-W_3^{\mathrm{el}}
\in\mathcal I_{\leq3}.
\]
Since \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\) is inverted in the multiplicative set \(S_W\) of Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}localization}\), division of this membership by \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\) gives
\[
\beta-\frac{W_3^{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}
=\frac{R_{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}
\in\mathcal I_{\leq3}^{(W)}.
\]

It remains to prove equality, rather than only containment, after passage to the observable function field.  Let \(\overline{\mathcal I}\) be the image of \(\mathcal I_{\leq3}\) in \(A[\beta]\).  The contraction identity in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}elimination\text{-}ideal}\) gives
\[
\overline{\mathcal I}\cap A=(0).
\]
Since \(\mathcal I_{\leq3}\) is prime, \(\overline{\mathcal I}\) is prime.  It is therefore disjoint from \(A\setminus\{0\}\), so localization at all nonzero observable classes produces a proper ideal
\[
\mathcal I_{\leq3}K_{\mathrm{obs}}[\beta]
\subsetneq K_{\mathrm{obs}}[\beta].
\]
The already proved nonvanishing of the class of \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\) and the relation above imply the containment
\[
\left\langle\beta-\frac{W_3^{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}\right\rangle
\subseteq \mathcal I_{\leq3}K_{\mathrm{obs}}[\beta].
\]
The ideal on the left is maximal: evaluation at
\(\beta=W_3^{\mathrm{el}}/W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\) gives an isomorphism
\[
K_{\mathrm{obs}}[\beta]\Big/
\left\langle\beta-\frac{W_3^{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}\right\rangle
\cong K_{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]
A proper ideal containing a maximal ideal equals it.  Consequently
\[
\mathcal I_{\leq3}K_{\mathrm{obs}}[\beta]
=\left\langle\beta-\frac{W_3^{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}\right\rangle.
\]
The generic \(\beta\)-fiber algebra is thus isomorphic to \(K_{\mathrm{obs}}\), so its dimension as a \(K_{\mathrm{obs}}\)-vector space, equivalently its generic degree, is exactly one.  Hence there is a unique generic full-system value
\[
\beta=\frac{W_3^{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}
\]
on the stated chart.  Tramontano et al. state generic nonidentification from the first three cumulants in \cite[Theorem~3.6]{tramontanoEtAl2025HigherOrderCumulants}, whose proof infers nonidentification from a retained degree-two elimination polynomial.  On the same moment map, the full localized ideal has instead the degree-one form just proved; a degree-two member can only be a multiple of this linear generator over \(K_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and cannot supply a second full-system root.  This is the asserted strict generic tightening.
